def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np
    steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (steps - 1)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0])
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1])
    time = 0.0

    points = np.empty((n_runs, steps, 3), dtype=float)
    points[:, 0, 0] = lat
    points[:, 0, 1] = lon
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0.0

    ok = np.full(n_runs, True, dtype=bool)

    # We move west: bearing = 270 deg = 3*pi/2 rad
    bearing = 3 * np.pi / 2

    for i in range(1, steps):
        elev0 = terrain.elev(lat, lon)
        # move one step in direction bearing, distance dt * speed
        # speed depends on slope between current and next point

        # initial guess: move cell_m meters west
        d_horiz = terrain.cell_m
        # compute next coordinates stepped west by cell_m
        lat_next, lon_next = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing, d_horiz)

        elev1 = terrain.elev(lat_next, lon_next)
        d_elev = elev1 - elev0

        # Compute walking speed with Tobler's function
        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, d_horiz)
        # Distance covered in dt seconds
        dist = speed * dt

        # Recalculate next locations with actual dist to move in bearing
        lat_next, lon_next = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing, dist)

        # Update only for runs still inside terrain
        inside_mask = terrain.inside(lat_next, lon_next)
        ok &= inside_mask

        # For runs leaving box, clamp their position so we do not go outside
        lat_next, lon_next = terrain.clamp(lat_next, lon_next)

        lat, lon = lat_next, lon_next
        time += dt
        points[:, i, 0] = lat
        points[:, i, 1] = lon
        points[:, i, 2] = time

    return points, ok
